durability_finding.class: a sealed artifact whose only durable-looking copies are under /tmp is one sweep from voiding a race day
durability_finding.correction_to_R496B_in_band: R-496 (B) says this sealed file 'existed in exactly ONE copy'. MEASURED at relocation time by enumerating every file of this name under /tmp and /home/yuqing: SIX byte-identical copies on six distinct inodes -- three under /tmp (fwd4, fwd5, fwd6), BE's own safety copy at ~/.local/state/pm-co/race_record_20260901_fwd5/ (taken in round 11 and recorded in Q-BE-236), the coordinator's ~/ctaNew_sealed_backup/ copy taken at 03:52:48Z, and this relocation's destination. THE DURABILITY ARGUMENT IS UNCHANGED and the count does not soften it: the three /tmp copies share one boot-time clear, so three are lost by the same event as one. What the count DOES change is the claim that the artifact was ever one sweep from being unrecoverable -- BE's round-11 safety copy outside /tmp already existed when R-496 (B) was written. Only the number and that inference are corrected; the relocation stands on its own reason, which is that a race artifact belongs at a canonical path a consumer can find, not in any operator's backup.
durability_finding.tmp_sweep_reading: systemd-tmpfiles: `D` clears /tmp's contents at boot and ages entries out after 30d. /tmp here is on the root filesystem, not a tmpfs -- so the exposure is the boot-time clear and the age-out, not volatility.
